key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings achieve better long-term corrosion and wear performance when droplets spread into dense, disk-like splats that minimize porosity.
engineering_relevance: Process parameters in detonation spraying can be tuned to improve coating density, corrosion durability, and humidity-dependent tribological performance on carbon steel components.
method: Fe-based amorphous coatings were deposited on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spray under different spraying parameters.
Corrosion behavior was evaluated over long-term exposure, and wear behavior was tested under different humidity environments using Si3N4 counterbodies.
Droplet morphology, circularity, expansion factor, and coating porosity were analyzed as microstructure indicators.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic corrosion and tribology testing, with results showing lower porosity linked to improved corrosion resistance and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases.
watch_item: Coating performance is sensitive to spraying-induced porosity and to environmental humidity, so process control and service-condition matching are critical.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
